These are two separate problems.

1. Local error: Unresolved reference 'awaitInstance'

awaitInstance isn’t a member of ProcessCameraProvider. CameraX adds it as a Kotlin extension function in camera-lifecycle (it’s been there since 1.4.0), so it needs its own import. In app/src/main/kotlin/io/github/terlingua/books/ui/transfer/QrScan.kt, add this next to the other CameraX imports:

kotlin
import androidx.camera.lifecycle.awaitInstance
Nothing else in that file needs to change.

2. CI error: KEYSTORE_PASSWORD has no value

The “Decode signing key” step writes TERLINGUA_KEYSTORE_FILE to $GITHUB_ENV, so every later Gradle step can see it. But KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, KEY_ALIAS and KEY_PASSWORD only exist in the “Build signed universal release APK” step. When :app:testDebugUnitTest runs, the build script finds the keystore file, creates the signing config, and calls .get() on a password that isn’t there.

The fix is to create the release signing config only when all four values are present. In app/build.gradle.kts, replace the keystoreFile line and the signingConfigs block:

kotlin
val keystoreFile = providers.environmentVariable("TERLINGUA_KEYSTORE_FILE")
val keystorePassword = providers.environmentVariable("KEYSTORE_PASSWORD")
val signingKeyAlias = providers.environmentVariable("KEY_ALIAS")
val signingKeyPassword = providers.environmentVariable("KEY_PASSWORD")
kotlin
    signingConfigs {
        val file = keystoreFile.orNull
        val storePass = keystorePassword.orNull
        val alias = signingKeyAlias.orNull
        val keyPass = signingKeyPassword.orNull
        if (file != null && storePass != null && alias != null && keyPass != null) {
            create("release") {
                storeFile = file(file)
                storePassword = storePass
                keyAlias = alias
                keyPassword = keyPass
            }
        }
    }
Your release { signingConfig = signingConfigs.findByName("release") } line already handles a missing config. The workflow doesn’t need changes: the test steps will now configure without signing, and the release step still gets all four values from its env:.

If a secret is ever missing, the APK comes out unsigned. The apksigner verify step in the release workflow then fails the job, so an unsigned APK can’t be published.

I couldn’t run a build here because this workspace can’t reach Google Maven. To check the fix locally, run ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest (and ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug) before you push.
